title: Pāhi no agna ekayā: protection by one, two, three and four
theme: A counting prayer to Agni: protect us with one, a second, a third and four songs of praise.

words.context: Anonymous: «एकयर्ग्वेदलक्षणया गिराऽभिष्ठुतः सन्» — praised with one, the Ṛgveda

words.role: joins the clause to the first

words.context: Anonymous: «द्वितीयया यजुर्वेदरूपा गिरा» — the second, the Yajurveda
Anonymous: «ऊर्जमन्नमन्नरसं च» — food and its essence
Anonymous: the Ṛg-, Yajur-, Sāma- and Atharvaveda
Anonymous: «हे वसो जगन्निवासहेतो» — cause of the world’s dwelling

sandhi.type: e before a vowel other than a
sandhi.rule: agne before e becomes agna, the y dropped, a gap left.
i becomes y before u: pāhy uta.

sandhi.type: i before a dissimilar vowel; m before a consonant
sandhi.rule: pāhi + ūrjam → pāhy ūrjaṃ (the m becomes anusvāra before t).

sandhi.type: visarga before c; visarga after i before a voiced consonant
sandhi.rule: gīrbhiḥ before c becomes gīrbhiś; catasṛbhiḥ before v becomes catasṛbhir.

sandhi_exceptions.note: no · agne: the a of agne is not elided after no, as in 10.6; every witness prints the two words apart.

morphology.note: Vedic: before a, naḥ is written no and the a of agne is not elided (classical no ’gne); the record declares the gap as a sandhi exception.
Feminine instrumentals of the ordinals, agreeing with an understood gir (song, word), which the last line supplies as gīrbhiḥ.

translation.literal: Protect us, O Agni, with one; protect [us] also with the second; protect [our] strength with the third; protect [us] with four songs, O good one — svāhā.
translation.readable: Agni, protect us with one song of praise, and with a second; with a third protect our nourishment; with all four songs protect us, good one. Svāhā.

syntax: Four imperative clauses with pāhi; the instruments are feminine ordinals (ekayā, dvitīyayā, tṛtīyayā) and finally gīrbhiś catasṛbhiḥ, which supplies the noun the others leave understood.

ambiguities.note: The text supplies gīrbhiḥ, songs, only in the last line. The anonymous commentator identifies them with the Ṛg-, Yajur-, Sāma- and Atharvaveda; the text itself does not name the Vedas.

metre.name: gāyatrī
metre.note: Counted 8, 7, 7 and 12 syllables: a gāyatrī-like triplet whose second and third pādas are one syllable short (pāhy uta dvitīyayā; pāhy ūrjaṃ tṛtīyayā), and a closing line of 10 + svāhā.

beginner: A short counting prayer to Agni, the fire: protect us with one, protect us with a second, protect our strength with a third, protect us with four songs of praise, good one. Only the last line says what is being counted, songs of praise. The anonymous commentator identifies the four with the four Vedas: the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda and the Atharvaveda, so that the god is protecting “us” as one praised by each Veda in turn and then by all. He says these are four offerings for the same purpose as the previous anuvāka, protection for one who seeks knowledge, and that svāhā belongs to each. The record reports that reading and claims nothing about its effect.
analogy: Like a child counting on its fingers, one, two, three, and then holding up the whole hand.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: It asks Agni to protect us with one, with a second, to protect our strength with a third, and to protect us with four songs of praise, ending with svāhā.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The anonymous commentator: four offerings for the same purpose as the last anuvāka («पुनरपि पूर्वोक्तप्रयोजनकाहुतिचतुष्टयमन्त्रा उच्यन्ते»), with Agni praised by the Ṛgveda («एकयर्ग्वेदलक्षणया गिराऽभिष्ठुतः सन्»), the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and by all four («चर्ग्यजुः सामाथर्वणरूपाभिश्चतसृभि[र्गीर्भिरभि]ष्टुतः»). Svāhā goes with every line («स्वाहाशब्दः सर्वत्रानुषज्यते»).

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: In पाह्यूर्जं the Ānandāśrama text writes an extra anusvāra (पाह्यूंर्ज), and both it and the Tirupati e-text lack the anusvāra the base gives ūrjaṃ before tṛtīyayā; the sources page lists these for review. Neither Sāyaṇa’s nor Bhāskara’s copy used here comments on this anuvāka.

schools.disagreement: Only the anonymous commentary comments on this anuvāka in the edition’s sources; it is ritual and takes no Vedānta-school position. No Viśiṣṭādvaita or Dvaita commentary on the Mahānārāyaṇa is in the edition’s sources (Raṅgarāmānuja’s is not available here).

contemporary.theme: Many ways of saying one thing
contemporary.text: The prayer asks the same thing four times, each time with one more voice, until all four speak together. Saying something important in more than one way, and then together, is how agreement is built. This is a modern reflection on the passage, not part of its traditional meaning.

reflect.beginner: Why might a prayer count up — one, two, three, four — instead of asking once?
reflect.deeper: The text names only “songs”; the commentator names the four Vedas. What does the identification add, and what does it assume?
reflect.practice: Say one thing you value in four different ways today: in words, in an action, in a gift of time, in silence.

references.text: Sāyaṇa’s anuvāka 5 (this edition’s 10.6) does not go on to this passage, and Bhāskara’s copy used here has no comment on it.

flags.note: In पाह्यूर्जं तृतीयया the Ānandāśrama text and the Tirupati e-text agree against the base on the anusvāra; listed for checking against a printed recitation text.
